insights: Shorts significantly outperform long-form videos, averaging over 1,000 views compared to under 100 views for long videos.

The 'Myth vs fact' content style yields exceptional viewer retention, demonstrated by the highest average view percentages on videos like the Artemis III Moon Rocket (113.9%) and Maglev Trains (90.5%).
Hook drop-offs frequently occur between 4.8 and 8.3 seconds into shorts, indicating that early script pacing in this window needs tightening.

Promotional call-outs at the end of shorts (e.g., pointing to the main channel or asking open-ended questions) cause noticeable audience drop-offs, suggesting end-screens and CTAs should be streamlined.
Data for long-form videos is currently too thin to draw firm structural conclusions, though they consistently suffer from low initial click-through and low view counts.
